Definition: from G3844 and G1391 (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, i.e. extraordinary ("paradox"):--strange.
BiblicalUsage: Paradoxos occurs once: after the paralytic is let down through the roof and rises and walks, amazement seizes them all, and they glorify God, saying, We have seen strange things to day.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that strange things are the right words for a miracle: a man carried in on a bed walks out on his own feet, and the crowd can only call it strange.
